source_text: Olim constitit de nominum proprietate, ei illam *, qui prior et Christum suum in homines adnuntiarit et legum transnominarit. constabit itaque et de impudentia eius, qui multos dicat uenturos in nomine ipsius, quod non sit ipsius, si non Christus et Iesus creatoris est, ad quem proprietas nominum pertinet. amplius et prohibeat eos recipi, quorum et ipse par sit, ut qui proinde in nomine uenit alieno: si non, ipsius erat a mendacio nominis praeuenire discipulos, qui per proprietatem nominis possidebat ueritatem eius. uenient denique illi dicentes: ego sum Christus: recipies eos, qui consimilem recepisti; nec hic enim in nomine suo uenit. quid nunc? quando et ipse ueniet nominum dominus, Christus et Iesus creatoris, reicies illum P et quam iniquum, quam iniustum et optimo deo indignum, ut non recipias eum in suo nomine uenientem, qui alium in nomine eius recepisti! Videamus et quae signa temporibus imponat: bella, opinor., et regnum super regnum et gentem super gentem et pestem et fames terraeque motus et formidines et prodigia de caelo, quae omnia seuero et atroci deo congruunt. haec cum adicit etiam oportere fieri, quem se praestat? destructorem an probatorem creatoris? cuius dispositiones confirmat impleri oportere, quas ut optimus tam tristes quam atroces abstulisset potius quam constituisset, si non ipsius fuissent ante haec autem persecutiones eis praedicat et passiones euenturas, in martyrium utique et in salutem. accipe praedicatum in Zacharia: dominus, inquit, omnipotens proteget eos et consument illos, et lapidabunt lapidibus fundae et bibent sanguinem illorum uelut uinum et replebunt pateras quasi altaris, et saluos eos faciet dominus illo die uelut oues, populum suum, quia lapides sancti uolutant. et ne putes haec in passiones praedicari, quae illos tot bellorum nomine ab allophylis manebant, respice ad species. nemo in praedicatione bellorum legitimis armis debellandorum lapidationem enumerat popularibus coetibus magis et inermi tumultui familiarem; nemo, tanta in bello sanguinis flumina paterarum capacitate metitur aut unius altaris cruentationi adaequat; nemo oues appellat eos, qui in bello armati et ipsi ex eadem feritate certantes cadunt, sed qui in sua proprietate atque patientia dedentes potius semetipsos quam uindicantes trucidantur. denique: quia lapides, inquit, sancti uolutant, non \'quia milites pugnant\'. lapides enim sunt et fundamenta, super quae nos aedificamur, exstructi secundum Paulum super fundamenta apostolorum, qui lapides sancti oppositi omnium offensui uolutant. et hic igitur ipse cogitari uetat, quid responderi oporteat apud tribunalia, qui et Balaae quod non cogitauerat, immo contra quam cogitauerat suggessit et Moysi causato linguae tarditatem os repromisit.
pass_a_gloss: Formerly it was established concerning the property of names, to Him, who first announced His Christ to men and changed the names of the laws. Therefore, it will also be established concerning His impudence, who says that many will come in His name, which is not His, if Christ is not the Creator's, to whom the property of names pertains. Moreover, He should prevent those from being received, whose equal He Himself is, so that He who comes in an alien name: if not, it was His to prevent His disciples from a lie of the name, who possessed the truth of the name through the property of the name. Finally, those will come saying: I am Christ: you will receive them, who have received a similar one; nor does this one come in His own name. What now? When the Lord Himself of the names, Christ and Jesus of the Creator, will come, will you reject Him? And how unjust, how iniquitous, and unworthy of the best God, that you do not receive Him coming in His own name, who have received another in His name! Let us see also what signs He imposes on the times: wars, I think, and kingdom upon kingdom and nation upon nation and pestilence and famine and earthquakes and terrors and prodigies from heaven, which all suit a severe and cruel God. Since He adds that it is also necessary for these things to happen, what kind of God does He show Himself to be? A destroyer or an approver of the Creator? Whose dispositions He confirms should be fulfilled, which the best God would have rather removed than established, if they were not His. But He predicts these persecutions and passions for them, which will happen in martyrdom and in salvation. Receive the prediction in Zachariah: the Lord, He says, Almighty will protect them and will consume them, and they will stone them with stones of a sling and will drink their blood like wine and will fill the bowls like an altar, and the Lord will save them on that day like sheep, His people, because the holy stones are rolled. And lest you think that these things are predicted for the passions, which they suffered in the name of wars from foreigners, look at the species. No one in the prediction of wars to be fought with legitimate arms enumerates stoning to popular assemblies and unarmed tumult; no one measures the rivers of blood in the capacity of bowls or equals the bloodshed of one altar; no one calls those who fall armed in war and fighting with the same ferocity sheep, but those who give themselves up rather than avenging themselves are slaughtered. Finally: because the holy stones are rolled, He says, not 'because the soldiers fight'. For the stones are also the foundations, upon which we are built, constructed according to Paul upon the foundations of the apostles, who are the holy stones opposed to every offense and rolled. And here, therefore, it is forbidden to think what should be responded to in the tribunals, who also suggested to Balaam what he had not thought, and to Moses promised a mouth, although he had a slow tongue.

pass_b_english: It was once settled that the authority over names belongs to the One who first announced His Christ to humanity and renamed the laws. So it will also be settled that the one who claims many will come in His name — a name that is not his if Christ and Jesus are not the Creator's, to whom the authority over names belongs — acts with sheer impudence. He should bar the reception of those whose equal he himself is, so that the one who comes in a borrowed name finds no welcome; otherwise, it was his duty to shield his disciples from the lie of that name, he who held the truth of the name by its very authority. In the end, men will come declaring, 'I am the Christ,' and you will receive them, since you have already accepted their counterpart; after all, this claimant does not come in his own name. What then? When the Lord of names Himself arrives — Christ and Jesus of the Creator — will you reject Him? How unjust, how wicked, and how unworthy of the best God, that you refuse to welcome Him coming in His own name, when you have welcomed another in that same name! Let us also examine the signs He assigns to the times: wars, I suspect, and kingdom rising against kingdom, nation against nation, pestilence, famine, earthquakes, terrors, and portents from heaven — all of which befit a severe and cruel God. Since He insists these things must happen, what sort of God does He reveal Himself to be: a destroyer or an approver of the Creator? He confirms that the Creator's own decrees must be fulfilled, decrees which the best God would have removed rather than established, if they were not His own. Yet He predicts these persecutions and sufferings for them, ordeals that lead to martyrdom and salvation. Take the prophecy in Zechariah: 'The Lord Almighty will protect them and consume them; they will stone them with slingstones and drink their blood like wine and fill the bowls like the corners of the altar, and the Lord will save them on that day like sheep, His people, because the holy stones are rolled.' Do not imagine these words forecast the sufferings they endured in so-called wars at the hands of foreigners; look at the details. No prophecy of wars fought with legitimate weapons lists stoning by popular mobs and unarmed tumults; no one measures rivers of blood by the capacity of bowls or equates the slaughter to a single altar's staining; no one calls those who fall armed in battle, fighting with equal ferocity, 'sheep' — but those who surrender themselves rather than retaliate, and are slaughtered in their innocence and patience. Finally: 'because the holy stones are rolled,' He says, not 'because soldiers fight.' For the stones are also the foundations on which we are built, constructed, as Paul says, on the foundation of the apostles — those holy stones, opposed to every offense, rolling on. And here, therefore, He forbids anxiety over what to answer before tribunals, He who suggested to Balaam what he had not thought — indeed, contrary to what he had thought — and who, because of Moses' slow tongue, promised him a mouth.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the 'property of names' and the distinction between the Creator and Christ. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version that maintains the nuances of the Latin (e.g., 'proprietatem' as 'authority' or 'property', 'species' as 'details' or 'kinds'). Scripture citation for Zechariah is correctly identified and applied to the quoted text.
